_metadata.rubric: owner-clarified rubric with calibration anchors + no-literal-false-facts reminder, 2026-10-18
_metadata.independence: I read only u28-blind-input.json; I opened no other file, ran no repository search, and used no web or paid API.

hints.reason: SNAKE is a Chinese zodiac animal (Year of the Snake); MOON reaches zodiac only via the lunar calendar behind that zodiac or the astrological 'moon sign', a secondary route.
Shape-only route: a crescent MOON is curved and a SNAKE curves as it moves, but the shared property is weak and points at many things.
MOON via the lunar cycle is strong; SNAKE needs the ouroboros (snake eating its tail as a symbol of the eternal cycle) or skin-shedding cycles, which most players will not reach.

best_available.why: Year of the Snake is a firm anchor and the lunar-calendar / moon-sign link is real, so it is the only hint where both sides are factual and themed together.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS; MOON+SNAKE has no familiar shared scene in this list. ZODIAC is closest and could be argued up to a moderate PASS via Lunar New Year.

hints.reason: SPIDER web is direct; MOON has no recognizable 'web' route.
MOON at night is strong; SPIDER only via many spiders hunting or spinning at night, which is true but not a salient association.

best_available.why: Only hint that touches both words, via a moonlit night when spiders are active.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS. WEB is spider-only; NIGHT leans on a weak nocturnal-spider link.

hints.reason: SPRING holiday; MOON because Easter's date is set by the first full moon after the spring equinox, a well-known piece of trivia.
MOON via the familiar 'rabbit in the moon' folklore (Mid-Autumn moon rabbit); SPRING via spring bunnies and the Easter bunny.
MOON drives the tides, and 'spring tide' is a standard compound (spring tides fall near new and full moon), so both sides meet in one fact.

best_available.why: 'Spring tide' is a real compound that is itself caused by the moon, giving a tight two-sided link.

pairs.pair_note: Strong pair: three valid routes, TIDE clearly best.

hints.reason: Express TRAIN is direct; MOON has no familiar 'express' route for a player.
MOON at night and the familiar 'night train' phrase; broad but both sides land.

best_available.why: 'Night train' is a familiar phrase and the moon is the night's emblem.

pairs.pair_note: Only NIGHT works; moderate strength.

hints.reason: Classic scene of the MOON reflected on still WATER.
WATER as ice is direct; MOON only via water ice detected in shadowed polar craters, true but not a player's association.
The MOON's pull makes the tides of the sea's WATER; textbook link.

best_available.why: Direct cause-and-effect fact everyone knows.

pairs.pair_note: Two strong routes; ICE is a factual but obscure moon link.

hints.reason: Halloween imagery pairs a big full MOON with a WITCH silhouette; both are stock Halloween symbols.
WITCH's broomstick, and the iconic image of a witch on a broomstick flying across the MOON.
Full MOON is direct; WITCH has no 'full' route beyond the moon itself.

best_available.why: Shared stock scene that names both images at once.

pairs.pair_note: Good pair; FULL is moon-only filler.

hints.reason: 'Twas the Night Before Christmas' with its 'not even a mouse' line ties both words in one famous poem.
Same poem: 'not a creature was stirring, not even a MOUSE' on that NIGHT; needs the poem but the poem is famous.
Mice are largely nocturnal, and nocturnal means active at NIGHT; shared-property route.

best_available.why: Famous poem naming both night and mouse.

pairs.pair_note: Strong pair; STIRRING depends on CHRISTMAS's poem.

hints.reason: Mouse pad is direct; OCEAN has no 'pad' route.
OCEAN ship is direct; MOUSE only via stowaway rodents aboard ships, where rats are the usual image.

best_available.why: The only hint touching both sides, via a ship's stowaway mice.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS; weak pair overall.

hints.reason: Mickey MOUSE is direct; PIRATE only via Disney's Pirates of the Caribbean or Mickey in pirate costume, a brand detour.
PIRATE ship is direct; MOUSE via ship-stowaway rodents (rats more typical) or Mickey's Steamboat Willie, both indirect.

best_available.why: Pirate side is strong and the stowaway-mouse image is at least a familiar scene.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS; both hints need a detour to reach one side.

hints.reason: Minnie MOUSE is direct; QUEEN only via Queen Minnie in the Kingdom Hearts games, which few players would reach.
Nursery rhyme 'Pussycat, Pussycat' where the cat visits the QUEEN and frightens a little MOUSE under her chair; one story covers both.

best_available.why: One well-known rhyme names both the queen and the mouse.

pairs.pair_note: PUSSYCAT is a good story route; MINNIE is mouse-only for most players.

hints.reason: Mousetrap is direct; RING has no familiar 'trap' route.
MOUSE click is direct; RING relates only as another sound word, not a connection.

best_available.why: Forced pick: at least sits in the computer/phone sound family alongside 'ring', though it reaches RING only loosely.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS; both hints are mouse-only.

hints.reason: ROBOT is mechanical; MOUSE via the wind-up mechanical mouse toy or the old mechanical (ball) computer mouse.
Computer MOUSE is direct; ROBOT via computer-controlled machines, a familiar tech-family link.

best_available.why: Computer mouse is instant and robots are computer-driven machines.

pairs.pair_note: Two moderate passes.

hints.reason: Mickey MOUSE is direct; ROCK has no familiar 'Mickey' route.
Mouse hole is direct; ROCK via holes in rock or the rock band Hole, neither a strong player association.

best_available.why: Mouse hole is iconic and holes in rock / the band Hole give a thin second side.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS.

hints.reason: MOUSE via the British children's books Brambly Hedge (a mouse community); ROSE only via brambles being thorny relatives in the rose family, which is a rescue explanation.
Rose garden is direct; MOUSE only as a garden visitor (field or garden mouse), a weak scene.

best_available.why: Both can plausibly be found in a garden; BRAMBLY is too niche.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS.

hints.reason: Salt lick is direct; MOUSE has no 'lick' route.
Shared kitchen scene: SALT is a pantry staple and a MOUSE raiding the pantry is a familiar image; moderate strength.

best_available.why: Only hint that places both in one recognizable scene.

pairs.pair_note: PANTRY is a moderate pass at best; could be argued down to BORDERLINE.

hints.reason: Mice scurry is a stock phrase; SHADOW only via literary 'scurrying shadows'.
SHADOW puppet is a direct compound; MOUSE only as one possible animal shape or a mouse hand puppet, not a standard pairing.

best_available.why: Shadow puppetry of small animals is a recognizable scene, though a mouse is not the iconic shape.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS; both are half-strong.

hints.reason: SHARK teeth are iconic; MOUSE via rodent gnawing teeth (and the tooth-collecting mouse of Spanish and French folklore); shared-property route at moderate strength.
Cat and MOUSE is direct; SHARK only via catsharks, a real but obscure shark family.

best_available.why: Teeth are a defining feature of both, if more famously the shark's.

pairs.pair_note: TEETH is a moderate pass; CAT is mouse-only for players.

hints.reason: Familiar scene of a SNAKE swallowing a MOUSE whole.
MOUSE is classic SNAKE prey; predator-prey route.
Pet SNAKEs are fed mice (feeder mice); recognizable feeding scene.

best_available.why: Most direct statement of the predator-prey relationship.

pairs.pair_note: Strong pair with three overlapping routes.

hints.reason: Shared property: both are unwanted household pests (mice strongly, spiders commonly).
Shared fear: the stock 'scared of mice' chair-standing image and the very common fear of spiders.
SPIDER web is direct; MOUSE only via using a computer mouse to browse the World Wide Web, a pun-like detour.

best_available.why: Clear shared category for both household creatures.

pairs.pair_note: Two moderate passes; WEB is a fun but indirect computer pun.

hints.reason: A SPRING snaps back; MOUSE via the spring-loaded mousetrap snapping shut.
Mousetrap is the compound, and the classic snap trap is driven by a SPRING (spring trap).

best_available.why: Mousetrap and spring trap converge on one object.

pairs.pair_note: Solid pair; SNAP depends on the trap image.

hints.reason: Hollywood STARs are direct; MOUSE only via Mickey Mouse's star on the Walk of Fame, which requires that detail.
Mickey MOUSE is direct; STAR only via Mickey being a cartoon star with a Walk of Fame star, a soft link.

best_available.why: Mickey as a famous screen star is the most findable route; HOLLYWOOD needs the same fact in reverse.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS; both hints rely on the same Mickey-as-a-star idea and could be argued up together.

hints.reason: TRAIN tunnel is direct; MOUSE via mice burrowing tunnels, a true shared-property route at moderate strength.
Mickey MOUSE is direct; TRAIN only via Disneyland's railroad or Walt Disney's love of trains, which players would not reach.

best_available.why: Both genuinely travel through tunnels.

pairs.pair_note: TUNNEL is a moderate pass; MICKEY is mouse-only.

hints.reason: WATER bottle is direct; MOUSE via the drip water bottle on a pet rodent cage, a scene more associated with hamsters.
WATER drip is direct; MOUSE only through the same cage-bottle explanation, one step further removed.

best_available.why: Pet-cage water bottle is a real if secondary scene for a pet mouse.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS.

hints.reason: WITCH casts spells; MOUSE only via stories of people turned into mice by a spell, which is the DAHL story without the anchor.
Roald Dahl's The Witches, where the WITCHes turn the boy into a MOUSE; one story covers both.

best_available.why: Famous book and films directly link witches and a boy turned mouse.

pairs.pair_note: DAHL is a good story route; SPELL is the weaker generic version.

hints.reason: A third animal: fox is a wolf's canid cousin and famously pounces on mice, but it relates to each word separately rather than linking them.
MOUSE as prey and WOLF as the archetypal predator stalking prey; predator-prey route, moderate on the wolf side.

best_available.why: Mouse is archetypal prey and wolf an archetypal predator.

pairs.pair_note: PREY is a moderate pass; FOX is a side-step.

hints.reason: Dark NIGHT is direct; OCEAN via the dark deep sea, a mood/property route that points at many things.
OCEAN tide is direct; NIGHT has no tide route of its own.
MOON lights the NIGHT and pulls the OCEAN's tides; also the moonlit-sea scene.

best_available.why: Strong link to both: night sky and ocean tides.

pairs.pair_note: MOON is clearly best; TIDE is ocean-only without the moon.

hints.reason: Black NIGHT is direct; PIRATE via the black flag, Blackbeard or the Black Pearl, a colour route rather than a shared scene.
PIRATEs raid ships and towns, and 'night raid' is a familiar phrase.
Lanterns light the NIGHT and hang on old PIRATE ships, but neither link is strong.

best_available.why: Pirate raid and night raid are both natural phrases.

pairs.pair_note: RAID is a moderate pass; BLACK could be argued up via Blackbeard/black flag.

hints.reason: 'Prom night' and 'prom queen' are both stock phrases.
Mozart's Magic Flute features the Queen of the Night; one famous role names both.
Drag QUEEN is direct, and a 'drag night' at a club is a familiar event.

best_available.why: Two equally familiar compounds.

pairs.pair_note: Strong pair.

hints.reason: Bells RING is direct; NIGHT has no familiar bell route ('night bell' is not a common phrase).
Engagement RING is direct; NIGHT only by imagining the proposal happening at night.
A PHONE rings; NIGHT via the familiar dread of a phone ringing in the middle of the night, a soft scene.

best_available.why: The late-night phone call is the only scene touching both sides.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS; all three hints are ring-led.

hints.reason: 'Night vision' is a compound; ROBOT via robot/machine vision and Marvel's android Vision; moderate strength.
NIGHT via night sentries on watch and ROBOT via sentry bots or guns in games and sci-fi; both links are secondary.

best_available.why: Night vision compound plus robot vision/Marvel's Vision.

pairs.pair_note: VISION is a moderate pass.

hints.reason: 'All night' is a phrase but ROCK needs a song lyric ('rock and roll all nite'); filler word rescued by an explanation.
Nightclub is a compound; ROCK via rock clubs where bands play.
Rock concert is a stock phrase, and concerts are a classic night out.

best_available.why: Nightclub compound plus rock club scene.

pairs.pair_note: Two moderate passes; ALL is filler.

hints.reason: The Bachelor's rose ceremony is iconic; NIGHT via the show's 'rose ceremony' nights and bachelor-party nights.
Prom night is a compound; ROSE via prom corsages and boutonnieres.

best_available.why: Prom night is instant and roses are a standard prom flower.

pairs.pair_note: Two moderate passes.

Road SALT is direct; NIGHT only via generic night driving, not a connection.

best_available.why: Forced pick: a night at sea is at least an image; ROAD is equally thin.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS; both hints are salt-only.

hints.reason: Moonlight fills the NIGHT and casts moon SHADOWs.
Shared mood: spooky night and spooky shadows are stock pairings; broad but both land.
Shared property: night is dark and a shadow is a dark area.

best_available.why: A specific scene linking both, not just a shared mood.

pairs.pair_note: Easy pair; DARK and SPOOKY are broad but valid.

hints.reason: Weeknight is a compound and Shark Week is a famous TV event.
SHARKs are archetypal hunters and many hunt at night; 'night hunt' is a natural phrase; moderate strength.

best_available.why: Two familiar compounds, weeknight and Shark Week.

pairs.pair_note: Good pair.

hints.reason: 'Night vision' compound; SNAKE via pit vipers sensing body heat in the dark, a well-known nature-documentary fact; moderate strength.
Nocturnal means NIGHT-active; many snakes are nocturnal, but snakes are not commonly thought of that way.

best_available.why: Night vision plus snakes' heat sensing gives a specific shared ability.

pairs.pair_note: VISION is a moderate, explanation-reliant pass; could be argued down to BORDERLINE.

hints.reason: Nocturnal means NIGHT-active; many spiders hunt or spin at night, but the spider side is not a salient association.
SPIDERs crawl, and 'nightcrawler' (the worm, the X-Men character) is a familiar compound.

best_available.why: Nightcrawler compound plus creepy-crawly spider.

pairs.pair_note: CRAWL is a moderate pass.

hints.reason: Spring equinox is a standard phrase, and at the equinox day and NIGHT are roughly equal (the word means 'equal night').
Spring peepers are North American frogs whose chorus is heard on spring NIGHTs; real but regional and niche.

best_available.why: Spring equinox is familiar and its day/night balance gives the night link.

pairs.pair_note: EQUINOX is a moderate pass; PEEPERS is a nice but niche route.

hints.reason: Stargazing is a compound, done at NIGHT.
Rule failure: STARRY contains the target STAR as a substring (would otherwise be 'Starry Night').
Van Gogh's The Starry Night names both the night and its swirling stars.
Night sky is a compound and stars fill the sky.

best_available.why: A single famous work titled with both ideas.

pairs.pair_note: Strong pair; STARRY must be removed for containing STAR.

hints.reason: Rule failure: MIDNIGHT contains the target NIGHT as a substring (would otherwise be 'Midnight Train to Georgia').
Sleeper TRAIN is a standard term, and sleeping is what you do at NIGHT (sleeper = overnight train).
Gladys Knight & the Pips' 'Midnight Train to Georgia' names the train and the night hour in one famous song.

best_available.why: Sleeper train is literally the night train.

pairs.pair_note: Good pair once MIDNIGHT (contains NIGHT) is removed.
